question: Which L2 regularization strength minimizes 5-fold CV Brier score in logistic regression?
rationale: Grid search over specified lambda values using exact 5-fold contiguous CV splits and standardized gradient descent (200 steps, lr=0.1) to minimize Brier score. This follows standard hyperparameter tuning methodology.
decision: Evaluate all five lambda values with exact specifications and select the one with lowest mean 5-fold CV Brier score
expected_effect: Will identify best regularization strength; expect improvement over baseline (lambda=0) if data exhibits overfitting tendencies, null effect if noise is minimal
falsifier: If all lambda values produce equivalent Brier scores (diff < 0.001), no single lambda dominates and the improvement metric becomes negligible

question: Do interaction features improve logistic regression performance with lambda=0.1?
alternatives: Add interaction terms x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3
rationale: Paired t-test across 5 CV folds comparing Brier scores with and without interactions is a standard statistical test for dependent samples. Threshold t > 2.0 provides conservative evidence.
decision: Augment feature set with 4 interaction terms, fit both raw and interaction models with lambda=0.1, compute paired t-statistic across 5 folds (raw Brier minus interaction Brier), report t-stat and interaction_helps=(t > 2.0)
expected_effect: Interaction terms may capture non-linear feature relationships; paired t-test may show significant improvement (t > 2.0) or no significant difference (t ≤ 2.0)
falsifier: If t-statistic computation fails due to singular fold distributions or all differences are zero, report observed t-stat and corresponding boolean

question: Which compression configuration (sparsity %, bits) best retains dense-model Brier performance?
rationale: Fit dense model on full dataset with lambda=0.1, then systematically apply sparsity (zero smallest-magnitude weights) and uniform quantization (map remaining weights to 2^bits levels). Retention metric (dense Brier / compressed Brier) measures performance preservation.
decision: For each of 6 compression configs: apply sparsity pruning (k=round(p*d) smallest weights zeroed), then uniform quantization on remaining weights. Compute in-sample Brier on full data. Select config with highest retention ratio.
expected_effect: Retention will decrease as sparsity increases and bits decrease. Optimal config balances compression (low retention) with usability (high retention). Best will likely be one of the less aggressive compression levels.
falsifier: If retention < 0.5 for all configs, model is severely degraded; if retention >= 0.95 for all configs, compression has negligible effect and most conservative config is optimal
